 Strategy shares fell 7.36% in premarket trading on Monday to $103.40, down $8.22 from Friday’s close of $111.62, as Bitcoin’s slide toward $62,000 over the weekend added further pressure on the MSTR stock price weighing on the largest corporate holder of the cryptocurrency. Executive Chairman Michael Saylor said on X that the dividend on Strategy’s Stretch preferred stock, STRC, will stay at 12% for December. STRC is a perpetual preferred share whose rate is adjusted monthly to keep it trading near its $100 face value. The rate has been 12% since July, up from 11.5%. STRC reached $100 on November 4 for the first time since May, after shareholders approved daily dividend payments, and closed at $99.91 on Friday. Not everyone agreed with the decision. A MSTR shareholder, called it a mistake, arguing that with a Federal Reserve rate hike now widely expected, a fixed 12% payout looks less attractive on roughly $8 billion of STRC outstanding.
